clue.text: Iron commitment ultimately put into state security

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word it follows, so only its closing letter is wanted
things put into something sit inside it, so these letters go inside the word for state

blocks.note: to state is to say
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the final letter of commitment

explanation.surface: A firm iron-clad pledge finally written into a nation's security arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: SAY opens up to take FE and T: SA(FE+T)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety and security are synonyms, both meaning freedom from danger or harm.

clue.text: Reduced depth in amendment of second law

indicators.note: an amendment changes what was written, so these letters are rewritten in another order

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for depth
all letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A legal amendment that cuts back the scope of a second statute.
explanation.walkthrough: D sits among the letters of SECOND LAW before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scaled-down has been made smaller in size or extent, the same as reduced.

clue.text: Delicate piece of cloth in folder

indicators.note: in places the cloth word inside the word for folder

blocks.note: a file is a folder for papers
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A fine fabric sample kept in a filing folder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile describes something easily broken or damaged, the same sense as delicate.

clue.text: Child, when tucked in, warm

indicators.note: something tucked in is pushed inside, so the word for when goes inside the word for child

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A little one is snug once tucked into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bedtime picture misleads: 'tucked in' is the container signal, and 'when' becomes a two-letter word meaning 'at the time that'.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast is to warm something before a fire, as in toasting your toes.

clue.text: Correct answer about cleric

blocks.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer
c. (circa) is the abbreviation for about
a curate is an assistant member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone is told their reply concerning a clergyman was right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it wants something to go around, but here it is simply C, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, accurate and correct are synonyms meaning free from error or mistake.

clue.text: Character at home with a burden accepting new one?

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the burden word takes the letter for new inside it

blocks.note: a card is an eccentric character
someone at home is in
taken as written
to be lumbered with something is to be burdened
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An oddball sitting at home, weighed down, takes on a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes in after the L of LUMBER to make NUMBER. The question mark shows 'one' is defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers such as one, two and three, so 'one' is an example.

clue.text: Comedian finally among us, mischievous kind

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it attaches to
a thing among others is surrounded by them, so the selected letter goes inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of comedian
elves are proverbially mischievous, so elfish means impish

explanation.surface: A comic finally joins us, a prankster type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like a noun meaning sort, but the definition is the adjective generous: U(N)S + ELFISH.
explanation.definitionFit: An unselfish person puts others first, which is to say they are kind and generous.

clue.text: Inability to remember bad men dividing continent

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the next word are disordered
something dividing a thing splits it in two by sitting in the middle of it

blocks.note: Asia is a continent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wicked men splitting a continent with no memory of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged men sit after the continent's first letter, splitting it in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for loss of memory, whether partial or total.

clue.text: Always this crossword? Not half

indicators.note: not half means half is missing, so the second half of the name is removed

blocks.note: this puzzle is the Everyman crossword

explanation.surface: A solver asks whether this puzzle is always like this, and gets the reply 'Not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' sounds like the British exclamation meaning 'very much so', but it tells you to drop half the puzzle's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times or always, as in 'ever faithful' or 'ever the optimist'.

clue.text: Painter showing variety of planet's scenery

indicators.note: a variety is a different version of something, so these letters appear in another order

blocks.note: every letter of these words, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a varied cosmic landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Stanley Spencer was an English painter, known for biblical scenes set in his Berkshire village of Cookham.

clue.text: Mineral starts to appear blue and silver in turn

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the opening letter of each following word is taken
in places the selected letters inside the word for turn

blocks.note: to turn into something is to alter
the first letters of appear, blue, and, silver

explanation.surface: A mineral that begins to shimmer blue and silver as it is rotated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' reads like 'one after another', but 'turn' is the verb change and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine-grained white form of gypsum, a soft mineral used for carving ornaments.

clue.text: Feeling essential to brass ensemble

indicators.note: something essential to a thing lies at its very core, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across the end of brass and the start of ensemble

explanation.surface: Emotion is the vital ingredient for a good brass band.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense is a feeling or awareness, as in a sense of dread or a sense of belonging.

clue.text: Text's aims lie in unravelling philosophy

indicators.note: unravelling undoes the threads of something, leaving the letters before it loose to be rewoven

blocks.note: every letter of these words, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A reader finds the purpose of a book only becomes clear as its philosophical argument unravels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie in' looks like 'consist in', but those words are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Existentialism is a twentieth-century school of philosophy associated with Sartre, centred on individual freedom and choice.

clue.text: Earlier group full of energy loudly followed by rising idol

indicators.note: a thing full of something holds it inside, so the group word encloses the other letters
in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the word for idol runs backwards

blocks.note: a band is a musical group
E is the symbol for energy
f (forte) is the musical direction for loudly
an idol is a hero

explanation.surface: A band, bursting with energy, plays loud, followed by its star rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Followed by' keeps the reversed idol after the energy and loudness letters, all still inside the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand is an adverb meaning in advance or at an earlier time.

clue.text: Charges to screen large fights

indicators.note: to screen something is to shield it by surrounding it, so the outer word wraps the other

blocks.note: dues are fees or charges paid
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone is charged to show big boxing bouts on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' feels like attacks in a fight, but it means fees: DUES around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Duels are formal fights between two people, so the plural noun matches fights directly.

clue.text: Rogue doctor absorbed by working on clues

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is taken inside it, so the doctor goes into the rearranged letters
letters that are working are being worked over and reshaped into a new order

blocks.note: all letters of these words
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A rascally medic absorbed in solving a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link meaning 'working on', but it belongs to the fodder with 'clues'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest or unscrupulous person, the same as a rogue.

clue.text: Trace idea reforms wipe out

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters before it are formed again in a new order

blocks.note: all nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A political notion about reforms wiping out every trace of what came before.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely, root and branch, which is what wiping out means.

clue.text: State endless desire, then deceive with misdeed

indicators.note: something endless has no end, so the final letter of the next word is cut off

blocks.note: a wish is a desire
to con someone is to deceive them
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Declare an unending craving, then trick someone with a wicked act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the verb 'declare' but it is the definition, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest by the Great Lakes.

clue.text: Today, surrounded by signs of approval, climbing mountain

indicators.note: something surrounded by another is enclosed within it, so the word for today goes inside
in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the signs of approval read backwards

blocks.note: nods are signs of agreement
now means at the present time, today

explanation.surface: A climber is cheered up a mountain today, with nods of encouragement all round.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the signs of approval climb; the word for today sits unreversed inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales, in the Snowdonia national park.

clue.text: Joint work about semi-aquatic mammal

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the word for work is read backwards

blocks.note: the hip is a body joint
op. (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: A joint study about a river-dwelling animal.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is opus, a numbered musical work; turned about it becomes PO.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippo, short for hippopotamus, is a large African mammal that spends its days in rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Quiet duck, truly wild fowl

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters before it run loose into a new order

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, so O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A silent duck, honestly a wild bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' and 'wild fowl' paint birds, but duck is O, a nil score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry is the collective word for domestic fowl such as chickens, ducks and geese.

clue.text: Opposing action from token ruler?

blocks.note: a counter is a token used in board games
a ruler is a measure for length

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: is a playing piece used for measuring a sort of countermove?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'ruler' is a measuring stick, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A countermeasure is a step taken to oppose or neutralise a threat, so it is literally opposing action.

clue.text: Shock upset father and friend

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for father reads upwards

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A dad and his mate both left reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal, but with only two letters it simply turns PA over.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, which is to shock someone deeply.

clue.text: End story in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it is heard, so the word for story is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: The finish of a story told at a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail of something is its rear part or end, as in the tail of a queue.

clue.text: Notice colour around snake

indicators.note: brought around means turned to face the other way, so the colour word runs backwards

blocks.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Spot the colours around a snake, the warning markings of a venomous one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but nothing goes inside; it turns the colour backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a kind of viper with zigzag markings.

clue.text: Queen with sign joined by secretary in court before artist

indicators.note: in puts the preceding letters inside the abbreviation for court

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A queen holding court with her star sign and her secretary, ahead of the court painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, so crosswords use it for any artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of Ptolemaic Egypt, famous for her alliances with Caesar and Mark Antony.

clue.text: Settle with noble publican

blocks.note: to land is to come to rest or settle
a lord is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Pay off a debt with an aristocratic innkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: A publican runs a pub, and in Britain the person behind the bar is traditionally called the landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's landlord is the licensee who keeps the house, which is exactly what a publican does.

clue.text: Performed unusually adeptly, short of time

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the following letters are arranged differently
being short of something means lacking it, so one letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A musician gave a surprisingly skilful performance despite running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop T from ADEPTLY, then rearrange the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Played and performed are both past tenses for acting a role or rendering music on stage.
